lead: This week's story of Abraham ends in peace. The king he once feared comes to him and says, “God is with you in all that you do”, and at a well the two men swear an oath. The Epistle (1 Timothy 4:1–5) guards the Fast against a false idea: “everything created by God is good”, so we fast out of love and not out of contempt for creation. In the Gospel, a crowd wants to keep Jesus to itself, and he says that he has been sent to other towns as well. In all three, God's purpose is wider than the place where we are standing.

set: The same Abimelech who appears in chapter 20, with whom Abraham began so badly, comes with the commander of his army. Water was life in the dry south, and a dug well was property worth fighting for. Abraham is a resident alien: he has no land of his own, and only the goodwill of others to protect him. This passage settles the question of a well and gives us the name of a place that will become important to the patriarchs (26:23–33; 28:10; 46:1).

The text speaks of “the land of the Philistines”. Many scholars note that the Philistines are known from history only at a later time, and think that the writer uses the name familiar to his own readers.
str: vv. 22–24: the king asks for an oath, and Abraham gives it.
vv. 25–26: the complaint about the well.
vv. 27–31: the covenant; the seven ewe lambs; the name of the place.
vv. 32–34: the king goes home; Abraham plants a tree, worships, and remains a stranger.
kw: Bĕ’ēr means well. Sheba‘ can mean seven, and it sounds like the verb for swearing an oath. The story plays on both: seven ewe lambs, and an oath.
Abimelech's word in verse 23: loyal, reliable kindness. It is one of the great words of the covenant, and it is striking to hear it here from the king.
This name for God occurs only here in the Old Testament in this form. Abraham owns nothing lasting in the land, and calls on the God who lasts.
vv: God is with you in all that you do
In 20:11 Abraham doubted that this place had any fear of God. Now its king says that God is with Abraham. Each has seen more of God in the other than he expected.
These seven ewe lambs you shall accept from my hand, in order that you may be a witness for me that I dug this well.
Abraham settles the dispute without force. A public gesture is his way to make peace and secure a right.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beer-sheba, and called there on the name of the Lord, the Everlasting God.
A tamarisk is a tree of dry places. To plant a tree in a land that is not yet his is a quiet act of hope.
And Abraham resided as an alien many days in the land of the Philistines.
The covenant over the well does not change his status. He is still a guest, and the promise of the land is still ahead.
ch: The Letter to the Hebrews says that Abraham “stayed for a time in the land he had been promised, as in a foreign land, living in tents” (Hebrews 11:9), because he was looking to the city whose builder is God (11:10). The Catechism draws on this praise of Abraham's faith (CCC 145). So the Church sees the believer as a pilgrim, who can plant trees and make peace with his neighbours here, while knowing that this is not his final home. That is a good description of Christian life, and of fasting too.

r.h: I was sent for this purpose
set: Luke has shown a first day of Jesus' work at Capernaum: the teaching in the synagogue, the man with the unclean spirit, Simon's mother-in-law, and the sick who were brought at sunset (4:31–41). Just before that, his own town of Nazareth tried to drive him out (4:16–30). Now the people of Capernaum try the opposite and want to hold on to him. Luke sets the two towns side by side, and neither gets to decide where Jesus goes.
str: v. 42: the deserted place; the crowd finds him and tries to keep him.
v. 43: his answer: other cities; “I was sent”.
kw: “It is necessary.” In Luke this little word marks what belongs to God's plan (2:49; 9:22; 24:26). It is why the mission goes on.
Verse 43 is the first time this phrase occurs in Luke's Gospel, and it is Jesus who says it. It means God's reign, and not first of all a place.
vv: At daybreak he departed and went into a deserted place.
After a long evening with the sick he seeks solitude. Luke often shows Jesus withdrawing, and elsewhere says that he went to pray (5:16). Mark's account says so here too (Mark 1:35).
and when they reached him, they wanted to prevent him from leaving them.
This is a natural and even loving wish. It is also a temptation. Even good people can want to keep Jesus for themselves.
But he said to them, “I must proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities also; for I was sent for this purpose.”
He knows who sent him and why. St Paul VI quotes this saying in his teaching on evangelization (Evangelii Nuntiandi 6).
So he continued proclaiming the message in the synagogues of Judea.
Here “Judea” seems to mean the whole land of the Jews, including Galilee, as in Luke 1:5. Some ancient manuscripts read “Galilee”, perhaps to make the geography easier.
ch: St Paul VI wrote that evangelizing is the grace and vocation proper to the Church, her deepest identity (Evangelii Nuntiandi 14). The Catechism teaches that everyone is called to enter the kingdom, and that the kingdom was first announced to the children of Israel and is meant to welcome people of all nations (CCC 543). A parish that keeps the Lord to itself has misunderstood him in the way the crowd did at Capernaum.

qa: If everything created is good, why do we fast?

Because we fast out of love and for freedom, and not because food or the body is bad. Today's Epistle warns against teachers who “forbid marriage and demand abstinence from foods” as if creation were evil (1 Timothy 4:3). The Church rejected that error from the beginning. In the Great Fast we give up good things for a time, to make room for prayer and to share with those who have less. Then we receive them again “with thanksgiving”.
study: Abraham made peace at a well with a man he had once misjudged. With whom could I settle an old dispute this Fast, at some cost to myself?
Do I want to keep Jesus to my own family, parish or community? Who are the “other cities” that need to hear of him from me?
